lens: FOUNDER FIT AND CLAUDE-LIKENESS. I checked each design against the founder's complaints of 2026-10-07: several AnA places on one screen; a right rail that is everywhere while AnA is sometimes in the middle; a right-hand canvas where documents are built live, can be pulled down, seen and edited; and features moved into apps instead of the client's workflow. I also asked whether each design would feel like using Claude with a canvas, and what a beta client would find confusing. I checked the cited claims against the repo at HEAD 5fa728ae4. Only one commit landed after 19fdc82c4, and it changed none of the cited files.

scores.strongest: It is the closest to claude.ai itself. AnA lives on one screen, the conversation. The canvas sits on its right with three states: closed, a Documents list scoped to 'This conversation' or 'This project', and an open document. The project page works like a Claude project page: a start composer, then Conversations, Documents and Files. It removes the rail outright, which is the most literal answer to 'right rail prevalent everywhere'. It keeps the D2 canvas that already works, including the .dcv-workbench wrapper whose comments overlay at 1500px or narrower really does apply (authoring-v2.css:1653-1666, DocumentCanvas.tsx:608). It also found the Recents privacy hole and the logo that goes to document-authoring (Shell.tsx:293-306, confirmed).
scores.fatal_or_serious: (1) The design says a person sees at most one AnA typing box, but on the conversation screen during a run there are still two. It never removes the run strip's 'Steer this run…' input (AnaWorkSections.tsx:538-553, mounted at ConversationThread.tsx:1350). That is the box the founder saw next to 'Reply to AnA' in screens.md shot 05. It also keeps the Live Drive steer box (LiveDriveOverlay.tsx:149-161). (2) 'Ask AnA about this' on Vault or Submission Center takes the person off the screen, so the record leaves view while AnA answers. AnA is never beside the client's work, which is the weakest answer to 'part of the natural workflow'. (3) In phase 1, DocumentAuthoring stays a full-width editor without AnA, and Vault 'Open in editor' still lands there until slice 13. A beta client therefore meets two document views for most of the series. (4) Live build is only a reveal: the canvas opens when artifact_draft arrives, which is after the tool has written the whole document. Streaming is slice 16 (size L, run last), and it names only stream.ts. stream.ts has no input_json_delta or partial_json handling; the fragments are buffered inside gateway.ts:2812-2815 (appendToolInputFragment). (5) It has no My work place (tasks go to the TaskTray), which conflicts with the CPO's PLACE decision for tasks.

scores.strongest: It folds the most work into the workflow. The project gets tabs: Overview · Documents · Review · Record · Submission. A document gets a lifecycle strip (Draft → In review → Approved → Filed → In submission) where the next governed action is the only primary button. Review is signed on the document itself: today ReviewTasksPanel.tsx:303-310 sends the reviewer to the task board, and Review.tsx:818's openEditor calls onNav('document-authoring') with no docId; both are confirmed. An end-to-end founder walk counts every navigation that leaves the project and must reach zero. AnA is one column in the same place on every screen. Both steer boxes go (A8, A9), as do the Home and Project composers and the W, E and R docks. Nav matches the CPO list (Home, Projects, My work, Vault, Submissions, Quality, Reporting).
scores.fatal_or_serious: (1) 'See the documents being built' is answered worst of the three. The design says the document 'fills in section by section as saved records arrive', but createDocumentFromDraft writes every section in one BEGIN transaction (authoring-from-draft.ts:231 onward), and stream.ts emits a single artifact_draft (around :2603). The document therefore appears whole, and token streaming is deferred outright. (2) It relies on Comments floating at 1500px or narrower (authoring-v2.css:1653-1666). That rule is scoped to `.dcv-workbench > .ed`, which exists only in DocumentCanvas.tsx:608, and B deletes that portal mode. On document-authoring the overlay starts only at 1204px or narrower (authoring-v2.css:44). At 1280px the canvas is about 824px against the editor's 940px floor, so the page scrolls sideways. (3) The AnA column is fixed at 400px with no divider, and there is no Recents in the sidebar, only a picker in the column header. Both feel less like Claude. (4) It keeps out-of-release or empty features as steps: the Path from program-journey, a dossier view, a Publish step, and AnA memory in the column menu. The CPO locks or scraps all of these, and a beta client would hit empty tabs.

scores.strongest: It is the most faithful to Claude with a canvas. The layout is sidebar | conversation | canvas, with the conversation centred when the canvas is empty. It has no top bar, a sidebar of New conversation, Search, Projects and Recents, a keyboard-operable resizable divider, and a ⤢ button to give the canvas full width. It is the only design with a real live build: it exposes the gateway's input_json_delta buffer (confirmed at gateway.ts:2812-2815) as artifact_delta, and shows the draft in the canvas marked 'Proposed by AnA · not saved'. The class-'confirm' approval (confirmed at tool-authorization.register.json:1770) renders on that proposal in the canvas, and an all-at-once fallback covers other providers. 'Ask AnA about this' attaches a chip and waits for Enter, as Claude does. A ratchet gate counts typing boxes (10 → 1), useAnaChat callers (5 → 1) and free-text asks (77 → 0; the 20 in quality/ are confirmed), so one AnA place stays enforced. AnA's write tools refuse when the canvas shows a different project; threads are already fixed to a project (threads.ts header, 'the project is fixed').
scores.fatal_or_serious: (1) Recents reads GET /api/chat/threads 'organisation-wide'. The global branch filters `WHERE t.organization_id = $1` with no user filter (server/routes/chat/threads.ts, around :96), so a beta client's sidebar would show colleagues' first messages. Design A's user_id scope is needed. (2) It makes the same Comments-overlay mistake as B: it deletes DocumentCanvas, and with it .dcv-workbench, the only place the 1500px rule applies. On DocumentAuthoring in a 984px or narrower canvas, Comments overflows between 1205 and 1500px (authoring-v2.css:44 versus :1653). (3) The nav has both 'Documents' (the authoring store) and 'Vault'. That gives a beta client two places to look for a document, and the CPO maps vault → Documents. (4) Its project and sequence tabs host surfaces the CPO scraps or locks, which a client would find empty or misleading: Dossier map (always empty), eCTD co-author, Publishing, Program journey and the Filings catalog. (5) It deletes the DocumentCanvas inline body and portal, which would be the sixth canvas generation. The founder personally directed the 2026-10-01 version. The design does re-pin ci:canvas-path, map D2's nine steps to tests, and show the founder slice 9 first.

lens: Regulated-product safety (21 CFR Part 11 / GxP). Scored on six things: governed acts (sign, freeze, approve, file to vault, controlled export) keep their reason, e-signature and audit; AnA proposes and the person decides, with no silent writes; a draft is always visibly distinct from a record; a downloaded working copy cannot pass for a controlled record; nothing streamed shows as saved; AnA cannot write into a project other than the one on screen. Verified against the repo at HEAD 5fa728ae4.

scores.strongest: It changes the fewest Part 11 paths and has the best project scope. The conversation screen holds the only AnA. The canvas stays DocumentCanvas inside ConversationThread, unchanged (DocumentCanvas.tsx:597-631). So the validated insert path keeps working as it is today: the EditorBridge from embedded.onEditorBridge (DocumentWorkbench.tsx:1344-1397), the model-admission gate anaInsertRefusal (ConversationThread.tsx:189-237), and per-turn authoringContext (ConversationThread.tsx:922-933). ask() continues a thread only within the same project and otherwise starts a new one. The status pill is always visible. Freeze, approve and e-sign keep the workbench ceremony. The export 409 is pinned by a regression test (verified at authoring.router.ts:5816-5840). It is the only design that fixes the Recents leak: the global thread list filters by organisation only and titles each row with the first user message (server/routes/chat/threads.ts:83-96), and A adds user_id.
scores.fatal_or_serious: (1) The working copy reuses the file-to-vault render. Its `notice` is a single statement printed before the content, on page one only (authoring-file-to-vault.ts:416; authoring-export.ts:56). renderAuthoringExport always builds the §11.50 signature manifest (prepareShared → signatureManifestLines). So a draft working copy that leaves the system could print 'Verification: this signature covers the content of this document', with nothing on pages 2 and after. That is the case the export 409 comment warns against. A names it only as a risk for QA/RA to review. (2) Streamed text (slice 16) is marked 'being written, not saved', but A does not say it is discarded when the confirm-class tool (tool-authorization.register.json:1770) is declined. The confirmation stays in the transcript, away from the text it confirms. (3) The hand-off auto-sends the origin context as a turn (slice 2) instead of attaching it and waiting for the person. (4) The project rule is client-side only. The server takes project_id from the request body (stream.ts:802, :887), and the draft tool writes there (authoring-draft-tool.ts:114). (5) Review's 'Sign in the authoring workspace' opens Authoring with no document (Review.tsx:587-589, :818). A's workflow says the reviewer lands on the document, but no slice changes that file. (6) The project Conversations list keeps the unfiltered program branch (threads.ts:43-63).

scores.strongest: It is the most conservative on live build: there is no token streaming. The canvas shows only saved records, the document is read-only while the turn runs, and the canvas never takes over an editor with unsaved edits. The lifecycle strip (Draft → In review → Approved → Filed → In submission) composes the existing governed components, which all exist: AssignReviewDialog, AuthoringFilingBar with EsignModal and reverify-signer.ts, FileToVaultDialog, AuthoringPlaceIntoFiling. It makes the next governed act the only primary button, and the disabled export says why. It is the only design that fixes signing without the document in view: ReviewTasksPanel.tsx:303-310 sends the signer to the task board, and Review.tsx:587-589 opens Authoring with no docId (both verified). It adds a D4 OQ test case for the working copy.
scores.fatal_or_serious: (1) The tracked-suggestion path breaks. B opens documents as `document-authoring`. DocumentAuthoring mounts the workbench with no `embedded` and no `onEditorBridge` (DocumentAuthoring.tsx:98-111), and the bridge is published only through embedded.onEditorBridge (DocumentWorkbench.tsx:1344-1397). So the column gets no insert target and no per-turn authoringContext (ConversationThread.tsx:914-933 builds both from that bridge). No slice wires it. Inserts fail closed, and people will paste instead. Pasted AnA text loses AnA's attribution (DocumentWorkbench.tsx:1328-1332), which is the ALCOA defect described at AuthoringAiDraft.tsx:13-18. (2) Cross-project writes are never addressed. The column persists across every screen and project, and the scope chip can read 'All projects'. The shell chat sends project_id = readShellProjectId() with the same thread_id on every turn (V2App.tsx:727-729; useAnaChat.ts:1093). The server never compares it with chat_threads.program_id, which is set only when the thread is created (chat-thread-helpers.ts:174-203). So a thread about project X drafts into project Y once Y is opened. (3) The working copy is a GET that writes a chained audit row, and the CSRF middleware exempts GET (server/middleware/csrf.ts:19, :83). A cross-site request can write a download audit row the person never made. (4) The project thread picker reuses the program branch with no user filter (threads.ts:43-63), which lists colleagues' first messages.

scores.strongest: It has the most complete Part 11 specification. (1) Working copy: POST, export permission required, a watermark on every page with id, version, status, user and UTC, no manifest, no export-history row, an audit hash, a document-control SOP definition and QA concurrence. (2) Streaming: shown as 'Proposed by AnA · not saved' with no download, file or edit actions; the confirm-class signoff renders on the proposal itself; it is discarded on decline; it falls back to today's behaviour when no fragments arrive. It verified the confirm class (tool-authorization.register.json:1770) and the gateway's fragment buffer (gateway.ts:2812). (3) It proves that a confirm given in the canvas writes the same chained D5 record. (4) 'Ask about this' attaches a chip and sends nothing until Enter, the strongest form of 'the person decides'. (5) It moves EditorBridge into a V2App context explicitly, so inserts survive the move. (6) It names D4 change control and the OQ re-runs.
scores.fatal_or_serious: (1) Its project-scope safeguard rests on a false premise and is not built. C says 'Threads are already fixed to one project (routes/chat/threads.ts)'. Only program_id is fixed, when the thread is created (chat-thread-helpers.ts:196-203). Each turn's project comes from the request body (stream.ts:802, :887), and the shell re-reads the open project every turn (V2App.tsx:727-729). A held confirm keeps the project from when it was held (stream.ts:2043). The 'write tools refuse on mismatch' rule appears only as a risk line; none of the 19 slices builds it. Yet C puts the one conversation beside every project's canvas. (2) Slice 2 puts the organisation-wide thread list in every sidebar (threads.ts:83-96: organisation filter only, title = first user message). Colleagues' message text becomes visible; opening one returns THREAD_FORBIDDEN (chat-thread-helpers.ts:145-147). (3) Slice 19 retires AuthoringAiDraft, the only path with span-level RAG source lineage (AuthoringAiDraft.tsx:1-20, used at DocumentWorkbench.tsx:4354). Its proof checks 'one drafting path', not that lineage is preserved. The replacement keeps attribution per turn, not per span (DocumentWorkbench.tsx:1333-1339, :3212-3220). (4) It makes the largest changes to validated code: it deletes the DocumentCanvas body, moves the bridge, and adds streaming in gateway.ts and stream.ts. (5) Freeze and Sign sit under ⋯.

graft: From C: (a) Working copy: a watermark on every page header and footer reading 'WORKING COPY — NOT A CONTROLLED RECORD · doc id · version · status · downloaded <UTC> by <user>'. Suppress the signature manifest for this mode, because renderAuthoringExport always builds it through prepareShared. Keep it a POST that requires the export permission. Add a document-control SOP definition and QA concurrence. (b) Streaming (A's slice 16): a 'Proposed by AnA · not saved' state with no download, file or edit actions. Render the draft_authoring_document signoff on the proposal in the canvas, discard on decline or failure, fall back to all-at-once when no fragments arrive, and prove that a canvas confirm writes the same chained D5 turn record. (c) Replace A's auto-sending hand-off with attach(ref): a chip above the composer, and nothing is sent until the person presses Enter. (d) A D4 change-control record, and re-run the affected OQ-AUTHORING steps after each shell slice. From C, hardened: enforce project scope on the server, for every write and confirm tool. Refuse when the turn's project_id differs from chat_threads.program_id (stream.ts:802 and 887 against chat-thread-helpers.ts:196-203), re-check at held-confirm time (stream.ts:2043), and offer 'New conversation in <project>'. From B: (e) Signing with the document in view. Review.tsx:587-589 should carry docId into the canvas, and ReviewTasksPanel.tsx:303-310 should sign in place through EsignModal with server reverify. (f) A lifecycle strip with the next governed act as the only primary button, and a disabled controlled export that states its reason. (g) The document is read-only while AnA's building turn runs. Also extend A's Recents user_id filter to the program branch (threads.ts:43-63). Finally, none of the three designs covers confirm-class tools that overwrite sections directly: update_protocol_section, write_kit_section and update_biosketch_section (tool-authorization.register.json). Whichever canvas hosts protocol-dev must refuse these while the section is open in an editor, or convert them to tracked suggestions.

lens: Engineering risk and time to a founder-visible demo in this repo (HEAD 5fa728ae4, concept2cure-v2). I counted slices to the founder's target layout in a browser, which slices can be reverted, which break CI gates (ci:canvas-path, tests/ui/one-shell.test.ts, the rail tests), how much test churn each causes, and the risk to turn records and governed sign-off. I checked the cited line ranges in V2App.tsx, Shell.tsx, ConversationThread.tsx, DocumentCanvas.tsx, DocumentWorkbench.tsx, app-v2.css, check-canvas-path.mjs, one-shell.test.ts, chat/threads.ts and surfaceActions.ts.

scores.strongest: Of the three, it needs the least rework to put the founder's target layout on screen. The conversation screen already has a document pane on the right. ConversationThread.tsx:1435 mounts `ct-canvas-pane`, DocumentCanvas.tsx:597-631 portals the one DocumentWorkbench into it, and V2App gives the shell column 0 width there through data-editor (app-v2.css:1374-1375). Slice 3, the auto-open, mostly means setting `expandedDocId` (ConversationThread.tsx:899) when a turn's authoringDoc arrives. It is client-only, can be reverted, and keeps all seven ci:canvas-path links unchanged. I checked them: thread mounts canvas (:124), canvas mounts workbench (:130), surface mounts workbench (:136), plus the tool, vault, file-to-vault and walk links. No renderer moves, no new grid, and window.C2C_CONVO stays (it is only extended). That matters because 12 source files and 24 test files use it. Turn records and sign-off keep rendering in the one host that already tests them (SignoffList, AnaActivity, conversationThreadSignoff.test.tsx). Run slice 3 first and the founder sees a document build on the right after one slice.
scores.fatal_or_serious:
Slice 2 is sized M but is really L.

(1) It deletes the rail (Shell.tsx:622-1548) and re-homes 14 test files in one commit. The design says '14 anaRail*.test.tsx'. Only 6 files match that pattern, but 14 test files under __tests__ reference AnaRail. shellAskGuard.test.tsx and liveDriveShell.test.tsx also assume a rail.

(2) The hand-off unmounts the origin screen. V2App.tsx:712-722 deliberately drops context that does not belong to the mounted surface. surfaceActions.ts:62-63 refuses actions the mounted surface has not registered. So the design's replacement for the 'What AnA can do here' chips ('AnA still receives screen_actions in the carried module_context') cannot run them. The only path is a Live Drive navigate-then-act, which takes the person off the conversation.

(3) Governed admin mutations leave the admin screen. one-shell.test.ts records that admin-console dropped ownsConversation precisely because the rail draws its §11.50 sign-off.

(4) 'Back restores Vault with its selection' has no mechanism. The surface remounts under a new bodyKey (V2App.tsx:1076-1078).

(5) Slice 3 also restyles .ct-side and the card action row (DocumentCanvas.tsx:528-593), so the four DocumentCanvas test files and conversationThreadCanvas.test.tsx will change. It also collides with the row 49/50 lane, which owns DocumentCanvas.

scores.strongest: Slice 2 is the cheapest visible change in any of the three designs. It swaps grid order and DOM order (.main is grid-column 2 at app-v2.css:1482, .ana is grid-column 3 at :1669) and sets anaOpen:true by default (V2App.tsx:179). That is mostly CSS, and reverting it is trivial.
